messages.subject: sampling from an arbitrary distribution
parts:
I am interested in sampling from a user-defined function that is proportional to the target distribution. For example, I know (and can define as a nimble function) f(x) = c Pr(x) and want a sample from Pr(x).

I have tried a user defined function df(x,y) with the nimble model y ~ df(x), a prior on x, and y initialized to either 0 or 1, but with no luck.

Is it possible to (ab)use a nimble model so that it will provide such a sample?

Thanks for your help.

Cheers,
Brook

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: sampling from an arbitrary distribution
parts:
Yes, this is quite doable, without too much effort.

From what you sent, it looks like you're attempting to generate samples for "y", is that correct?  And, that y is discrete-valued?  If so, then you'll need to register your distribution as being discrete, as shown below.

Also, make sure to *not* name the argument to your distribution as "x".  In the custom distribution definition, that name "x" is reserved for the variate which is following the distribution.  Here, below, I'm calling the single argument "arg"

registerDistributions(
    list(dmydist = list(
             BUGSdist = 'df(arg)',
             discrete = TRUE    ## necessary if distribution is discrete-valued
         ))
)

Also, is there any data in your model?  If not, then it would actually use a posterior predictive sampler, which would try to find the random generation r-function.  We can work around that if there's no data, but it would make a bit of a difference.

If you're able to provide the code you tried - including the model code itself, and your nimbleFunction definition of df() - then it won't be too much trouble to get it working.

Cheers,
Daniel

I have attached some Nimble code. I did get this to work, but would appreciate feedback on whether or not this is the “best” way forward.

I have an arbitrary function f() (apparently no need to register?) taking a single argument x (besides log) and want a sample of x from a distribution proportional to f(). Using

p <- f(x)
one ~ dbern(p)

seems to provide the needed sample.

Is this the general solution for sampling from any arbitrary function, at least as long as 0 <= f() <=1? Are there better or more appropriate approaches?

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: sampling from an arbitrary distribution
parts:
I guess there are many ways to approach this problem.  What you did works fine, and below is another approach which felt more natural to me - no need to introduce the Bernoulli distribution, or the "one" data.  Also, this no longer requires your function to be scaled down to attain values between 0 and 1.  Any (strictly non-negative, proportional) function will be fine.

Also, there was not even a possibility of "registration" of the distribution in your example, since it wasn't a "custom distribution", but rather a custom (deterministic) function.  Below, I actually use a custom *distribution*, called dfun, which gets automatically registered at the time of model building.

There's just a few comments in the code, but feel free to ask questions if anything is unclear.

Cheers!
Daniel

library(nimble)

## changed name to 'dfun' to avoid conflict with R's rf() function
dfun <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(x = double(0), log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
        returnType(double(0))
        pdf <- -8 * x * (x-1)
        ####pdf <- pdf / 2      # pdf(x) <= 1 for all x  --- no longer necessary
        if(log) return(log(pdf))
        else return(pdf)
    })

code <- nimbleCode({
    x ~ dfun()
})

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, inits = list(x = 0.5))

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)
conf$replaceSampler('x', 'RW')    ## need to replace the default predictive sampler with a RW sampler

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)

Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

mcmc.out <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, 100000)
